title: Double-counit identification in an etale-horizontal square
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}R'&\xrightarrow{e'}&R\\ h'\downarrow&&\downarrow h\\ T'&\xrightarrow e&T\end{array}$$
be a Cartesian square of Noetherian schemes, meaning schemes admitting finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Assume every arrow is separated and finite type, the horizontal arrows $e,e'$ are etale, and give the arrows and their equal composites $he'=eh'$ compactifications [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Work in ordinary unbounded small-etale constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $F_a=Ra_!\dashv G_a$ with counit $\varepsilon_a$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. For $a=e,e'$, put $S_a=D(a_{\Sigma!})\dashv a^*$ with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_a$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], take $d_a:F_a\xrightarrow{\sim}S_a$ from the proper-support/sum comparison [lem-sfb-quasifinite-compact-support-exact], and put $\rho_a=(d_a^{-1})^c:G_a\xrightarrow{\sim}a^*$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\alpha_{b,a}:F_bF_a\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{ba}$ and $C:e^*F_h\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{h'}e'^*$ be the specified compact-support compositor and exchange [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and let $c_{b,a}:G_{ba}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_aG_b$ be the conjugate of $\alpha_{b,a}$ under the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Define
$$\delta=(d_eF_{h'})\alpha_{e,h'}^{-1}\alpha_{h,e'}F_h(d_{e'}^{-1}):F_hS_{e'}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_eF_{h'}.$$
For every $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ define the isomorphism
$$b_K=G_{h'}(\rho_{e,K})c_{e,h',K}c_{h,e',K}^{-1}\rho_{e',G_hK}^{-1}:e'^*G_hK\longrightarrow G_{h'}e^*K.$$
Writing $t_K=\varepsilon_{h,K}$ and $t'_K=\varepsilon_{h',e^*K}$, its composite counit satisfies the equality of maps $S_eF_{h'}e'^*G_hK\to K$
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e(t'_K\circ F_{h'}b_K)=t_K\circ F_h(\operatorname{ev}_{e',G_hK})\circ\delta_{e'^*G_hK}^{-1}.$$
Moreover its single counit is
$$t'_K\circ F_{h'}b_K=e^*(t_K)\circ C_{G_hK}^{-1}:F_{h'}e'^*G_hK\longrightarrow e^*K.$$
Thus $b_K$ is exactly the $F_{h'}\dashv G_{h'}$ adjunct of the displayed inverse-exchange/counit composite. These equalities hold for the specified maps, are natural in $K$, and commute with proper-refinement comparisons and further compatible Cartesian open restriction; right-adjoint restriction comparisons here are those determined by the compact-support exchange and the same normalized sum/evaluation adjunctions. No smoothness or purity assertion is assumed.

source.place: Step 1: composite-counit expansion and the two adjunction cancellations identifying Cartesian base change

proof.text:
Fix the adjunctions in the statement. We use the transpose rule $\operatorname{adj}^{-1}(x)=\varepsilon\circ L(x)$ and its injectivity. In particular, for $\tau:L_2\to L_1$, the definition of conjugacy gives
$$\varepsilon_{2,K}\circ L_2(\tau^c_K)=\varepsilon_{1,K}\circ\tau_{R_1K}.$$
Indeed, $\tau^c_K$ is by definition the adjunct of the right side under $L_2\dashv R_2$. Taking $\tau=d_a^{-1}:S_a\to F_a$ therefore gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{a,K}\circ S_a(\rho_{a,K})=\varepsilon_{a,K}\circ d_{a,G_aK}^{-1}.$$
This fixes the counit normalization, including its direction, for both $a=e,e'$.

source.place: Definition 0037 (definition-adjoint), transpose formulas after the definition; conjugate specialization

proof.text:
Put $L_1=F_hF_{e'}$, $R_1=G_{e'}G_h$, $L_2=F_eF_{h'}$, and $R_2=G_{h'}G_e$, using the composite adjunctions. The equality $he'=eh'$ lets us use one functor $F_{he'}=F_{eh'}$. Define
$$\tau=\alpha_{h,e'}^{-1}\circ\alpha_{e,h'}:L_2\longrightarrow L_1.$$
Contravariant composition of conjugates gives
$$\tau^c=c_{e,h'}\circ c_{h,e'}^{-1}:R_1\longrightarrow R_2.$$
Here $\alpha_{h,e'}^c=c_{h,e'}$ and $\alpha_{e,h'}^c=c_{e,h'}$ by the specified definitions, so the formula follows by first conjugating $\alpha_{h,e'}^{-1}$ and then $\alpha_{e,h'}$. No claim about geometric base change is used in this calculation.

source.place: conjugateEquiv_comp, conjugateEquiv_id, conjugateIsoEquiv; composite adjunction counit as in Stacks 0DV0

proof.text:
Replace the etale left adjoints by $S_{e'},S_e$. The left-adjoint composite becomes
$$\widehat\tau=F_h(d_{e'})\circ\tau\circ(d_e^{-1}F_{h'}) : S_eF_{h'}\longrightarrow F_hS_{e'}.$$
Inverting the four factors defining $\delta$ shows $\widehat\tau=\delta^{-1}$. Under $F_hS_{e'}\dashv e'^*G_h$ and $S_eF_{h'}\dashv G_{h'}e^*$, mate pasting for a change of adjunction identifies its conjugate as
$$\widehat\tau^c_K=G_{h'}(\rho_{e,K})\circ\tau^c_K\circ\rho_{e',G_hK}^{-1}=b_K.$$
To check the two normalization factors: the conjugate of $d_e^{-1}F_{h'}$ is $G_{h'}\rho_e$, whereas the conjugate of $F_h d_{e'}$ is $\rho_{e'}^{-1}G_h$. This is the composite-adjunction pasting rule, followed by contravariant composition. Every factor is an isomorphism by conjugacy, so $b$ is an isomorphism of functors.

For the normalized composite adjunctions of Step 3 the two counits are, respectively,
$$t_K\circ F_h(\operatorname{ev}_{e',G_hK}),\qquad
\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e(t'_K).$$
Apply the conjugate transpose identity from Step 1 to $\widehat\tau=\delta^{-1}$ and $\widehat\tau^c=b$. It reads
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e(t'_K)\circ S_eF_{h'}(b_K)=t_K\circ F_h(\operatorname{ev}_{e',G_hK})\circ\delta^{-1}_{e'^*G_hK}.$$
Functoriality of $S_e$ combines its two rightmost factors on the left into $S_e(t'_K\circ F_{h'}b_K)$. This is the asserted double-counit equality, with domain $S_eF_{h'}e'^*G_hK$.

Apply the existing etale-horizontal support-mate identity with $(f,f',u,u')=(h,h',e,e')$ and $M=G_hK$. Its $d$, $\alpha$, $\delta$, and $C$ are exactly the ones specified here, not replacements with the same endpoints. All its hypotheses hold: finite commutative coefficients, Noetherian schemes, separated finite-type arrows, etale horizontal arrows, and compactifications of the arrows and equal composites. It gives
$$F_h(\operatorname{ev}_{e',G_hK})\circ\delta^{-1}_{e'^*G_hK}
=\operatorname{ev}_{e,F_hG_hK}\circ S_e(C^{-1}_{G_hK}).$$
After postcomposing with $t_K$, naturality of the evaluation counit for $t_K:F_hG_hK\to K$ changes the right side into
$$\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e\bigl(e^*(t_K)\circ C^{-1}_{G_hK}\bigr).$$
Thus Step 4 and this identity express two equal maps as inverse transposes under $S_e\dashv e^*$.

source.place: Tags 0F7J/0F7K: specified compositor; etale-horizontal support-mate identity (existing DAG node), then counit naturality

proof.text:
Set $N=F_{h'}e'^*G_hK$. The inverse transpose map
$$\operatorname{Hom}(N,e^*K)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(S_eN,K),\qquad x\longmapsto\operatorname{ev}_{e,K}\circ S_e(x)$$
is injective because it is the inverse adjunction bijection. Cancelling this bijection in Steps 4 and 5 yields
$$t'_K\circ F_{h'}(b_K)=e^*(t_K)\circ C^{-1}_{G_hK}.$$
Applying the $F_{h'}\dashv G_{h'}$ bijection identifies $b_K$ as the unique adjunct claimed. Every factor in the displayed expression for $b$ is a natural transformation, so their composition is natural in $K$; the equations just proved are equations of those natural transformations. This argument does not cancel $S_e$ as a faithful functor or assume either evaluation counit is invertible.

source.place: Definition 0037 (definition-adjoint), inverse transpose formula and bijectivity

proof.text: For a change of compactification, identify the left adjoints by their proper-refinement comparisons. The comparison theorem says that $\alpha$ and $C$ agree under these identifications, and the quasi-finite comparison theorem says that $d_e,d_{e'}$ do also. For example, if $r_a:F_a^c\to F_a^{\tilde c}$, then $d_a^c=d_a^{\tilde c}\circ r_a$; substituting this and the corresponding compositor square into the four factors of $\delta$ cancels each adjacent $r_a,r_a^{-1}$. Thus $\delta$ agrees. The right-adjoint comparisons are the conjugates of the inverse $r_a$. By the change-of-adjunction pasting rule these same substitutions into $\widehat\tau^c=b$ give the right-adjoint comparison square for $b$. The defining transpose identity preserves the counits as in Step 1. Consequently both counit equalities, including their normalization, agree under refinement. The cocycle identity for the left comparisons and contravariant composition give independence of a common refinement on both sides.

source.place: Tags 0F7I/0F7J/0F7K and 0GKM: refinement and composition of the specified comparisons; conjugate pasting

proof.text:
Finally consider a further compatible Cartesian open restriction. For a vertical arrow $a:Z\to W$ and its restricted arrow $\bar a:\bar Z\to\bar W$, with open maps $j_Z,j_W$, denote the inverse exchange by $E_a:F_{\bar a}j_Z^*\to j_W^*F_a$. Its mate $r_a:j_Z^*G_a\to G_{\bar a}j_W^*$ is precisely the right-adjoint restriction comparison specified in the question; its counit equation is
$$\varepsilon_{\bar a,j_W^*K}\circ F_{\bar a}(r_{a,K})=j_W^*(\varepsilon_{a,K})\circ E_{a,G_aK}.$$
The comparison theorem's compatibility of $C$ with successive changes of base gives equality of the two pasted inverse-exchange squares obtained by first restricting our square or first applying its horizontal exchange. Apply mate pasting along the intervening functors to that equality. Its two mates are the two paths comparing the restriction of $b$ with $\bar b$, since Step 6 identifies $b$ with the mate of $C^{-1}$. Hence their comparison square commutes. This also identifies both counit formulas after restriction, by the displayed counit equation. The normalization uses the same sum adjunctions: clause (1) of the etale support-map compatibility intertwines $d_a$ with the specified sum-extension base-change comparison. Restricting a sum/evaluation counit evaluates each restricted lift, the same operation as restricting its evaluated section; thus this comparison preserves evaluation, degreewise and hence on the stated termwise derived adjunctions. No new smoothness or purity input is involved.
